Learning a language is a science; speaking it is an art.

Every book we use in class was written by us. They grew out of research in applied linguistics and out of our lessons in Assisi: from students' mistakes, from the questions that have kept coming back for more than thirty years. The course we use today, In italiano. Il corso, is published by Hoepli.

Start from the situation

You learn a language by using it: introducing yourself, asking, telling, discussing. Grammar, too, grows out of use, within a given context. That is why our approach is communicative and situational: you start from a concrete situation and learn to handle it in Italian.

Few structures, many sentences

Grammar follows a principle of generativity: a few structures, presented in their natural order, from which many others follow.

First the words you use

Vocabulary is chosen by frequency of use, so you learn first what you will actually use.

Pronunciation has its own space

Dedicated exercises on the sounds that are hardest to hear and to produce, with pronunciation lessons every week.

Contrastive grammars

Lessons are taught in Italian. For individual study, contrastive grammars are available in fifteen languages, from English to Chinese, from Russian to Arabic, comparing the structures of Italian with those of your mother tongue.

Texts for specific needs

Alongside the course there are texts for specific needs: 19th- and 20th-century literature, graded tests for certification, and Italiano in chiesa for seminarians and religious.

The authors of the method, Angelo and Gaia Chiuchiù, direct the courses: they design the programmes and follow the work in class. Studying here means studying with the people who wrote the books and who test them every day in the classroom.
